data.title: Vaidehee Chaudhari wins third Fenesta Open title; Maan Kesharwani claims maiden men's crown
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Top seed Vaidehee Chaudhari and sixth seed Maan Kesharwani clinched the women's and men's singles titles, respectively, at the 31st Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship at the DLTA Complex in New Delhi on Saturday.

Chaudhari, who also won the title in 2022 and 2024, defeated 20-year-old Shruti Ahlawat 6-4, 7-5 in a closely contested final that lasted two hours and 15 minutes to secure her third Fenesta Open crown.

"I feel so proud. This is my third title so definitely I am very happy right now," Chaudhari said after the win, as per a press release.

"The first set I was 5-3 up and she kept fighting. Even the second set, I was 5-3 up and she kept fighting till the end. It was a great and a close match," she said.

In the men's singles final, Kesharwani defeated third seed Nitin Sinha 6-0, 6-4 in one hour and 37 minutes to claim his maiden Fenesta Open title.

Kesharwani made a dominant start, winning the first six games to take the opening set without dropping a game. The second set was more competitive, but the sixth seed secured a crucial break at 3-2 before holding his serve to close out the match.

"The first set was easy. But I will congratulate my opponent," Kesharwani said.

"He is a little bit injured but still he is playing and competing. So proud of him. In the second set, it was a little bit shaky. But at 3-2, I broke him, and then I was just holding my serves and I won. This is my first Fenesta title. Since the last 4 years, I was losing in the first round in every Fenesta Open. This time I directly made the finals and won. I am very emotional. I do not know how to express it in words but I am so happy. I would like to specially thank my parents, who have always supported me."

The presentation ceremony was attended by Rohit Rajpal, president of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association; Saket Jain, Executive Director and Business Head, Fenesta Building Systems; Indian hockey player and 2026 Asian Games gold medallist Jugraj Singh; and Prerna Bhambri, a four-time Fenesta Open champion and treasurer of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA). They presented the trophies to the winners.

"I am very happy to be here," Singh said after the presentation ceremony. "This is the first time I am watching a live match of the Tennis Nationals. I saw a lot of movement in these matches as well. Their shots, receiving the ball and their footwork, I was very happy to watch the matches. I want to say good luck to all the players who have won and to all the others who participates."

Jain reflected on DCM Shriram's nearly three-decade association with Indian tennis through the Fenesta Open and highlighted the company's continued commitment to player development.

"At DCM Shriram, we deeply believe in this journey of growth," he said. "Our association with Indian tennis through the Fenesta Open spans over three decades. Over the years, this championship has been about more than organising a tournament. It has been about creating opportunities, nurturing talent and providing Indian players with a platform to test themselves, gain exposure and take the next step in their sporting careers. That is why we are taking our commitment a step further this year."

"In addition to the championship prize money, we have introduced an additional Rs 11 lakh Player Development Scholarship from our CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) budgets to support the winners and runners-up in their journey ahead. The scholarship will help players invest in essential aspects of their development, including coaching, physiotherapy, fitness and tennis equipment. We hope this initiative helps players invest in their development and pursue their aspirations with greater confidence," he added.

Sixteen-year-old Ribhav Saroha, the 10th seed, upset fourth seed Om Ramesh Patel 6-4, 6-3 to win the boys' U-18 singles title.

"I have played Om many times before and before this match our head-to-head was 3-3. I knew that he is a guy who does not miss any ball and I have to work really really hard. I was really prepared that I have to work the balls and I have to be more consistent than him and I have to be aggressive as well. I played really well and I had a strategy to be consistent and aggressive at the same time. I was able to maintain that strategy," said Saroha.

Reflecting on his experience at the DLTA, Saroha said, "I played Fenesta three years ago for the first time and I played the qualifying of the U14s and for me it is like the Indian Grand Slam. The facilities are really superb and everything is on the mark. It's really excellent to play on these courts and I feel so happy to win this U18 Fenesta Nationals being a 16-year-old."

In the girls' U-18 singles final, second seed Parthsarthi Mundhe defeated seventh seed Aahan Aahan 6-3, 6-4 to lift the title.

"It was not a very easy match but it was a good one," Mundhe said after the win. "She was rallying and there were long rallies in the match. This tournament has been a very good experience actually. This is my first tournament after five months. It was a very great experience that I reached the finals and could win it."

The action now shifts to the Fenesta Open U-16 and U-14 events, which kick off next week at DLTA.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Says French Debt Crisis Could Send Bitcoin To $250,000 As AI Debt Risks Mount
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arthur Hayes said he thinks a French financial crisis could force the Fed and Treasury to manufacture money, pushing Bitcoin higher.
  • France's 10-year government bond yield momentarily exceeded 5% on October 1 and 2, its highest level since 2002.
  • If the crisis scenario develops, Hayes anticipates Bitcoin to trade between $125,000 and $250,000 by year-end.

Arthur Hayes believes that problems in France's bond market could propel Bitcoin (BTC) to a new high. The BitMEX co-founder stated that a French debt crisis would push the Fed and U.S. Treasury to issue money.

Hayes, speaking after his TOKEN2049 Singapore speech with CryptoBanter on Thursday, labeled France the weak link, cited its high government expenditure in relation to the size of its economy, claiming that few investors want its debt. Bond markets are already under stress. France's 10-year yield momentarily surpassed 5% on October 1 and 2, the highest level since 2002.

Its premium over German bonds has increased to approximately 152 basis points, the highest since 2011. The government intends to borrow a record €340 billion next year. Yields have dipped since then, although they remain about 4.8%.

In such a scenario, Bitcoin could benefit with the low end being close to Bitcoin's previous record of approximately $126,000, seen in October last year. He believes Bitcoin will trade between $125,000 and $250,000 before the end of the year if that case holds out.

Bitcoin’s price was trading at around $82,751, down 0.5% in the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, as chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Could Help US Retire Its Entire Treasury Debt?

Hayes said the U.S. would respond with a gold revaluation. “I would monetize gold and essentially depreciate the dollar against gold,” he said. He said he would set the price for gold at $50,000 to $60,000 per ounce.

The gain would allow Washington to retire the whole stock of Treasury securities. Hayes predicted that the move would be significantly inflationary. He described it as the only method he sees to deal with excessive debt and high interest payments.

Hayes Warns AI Data Center Debt Could Trigger A 2008-Style Crisis

Hayes also finds risk in investing in AI. The U.S. economy is so heavily dependent on building data centers, they’re like real estate projects, he said. That means if tenants can’t pay, lenders will cease financing new developments.

The waste could become obvious in 2027 and 2028, he said. Bad debt could then extend to insurers and fiduciaries, as it happened in 2008. Hayes anticipates governments will print money to make insurers whole, rather than allow AI to cause a recession.

Soaring sovereign yields are squeezing out AI funding, he said. Hyperscalers care less about the increased costs of debt because they see the benefit of constructing advanced AI as endless, Hayes said. Countries like France are the ones that are squeezed.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Procter & Gamble, Palantir and SentinelOne among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the green on Friday, with Nasdaq and Dow advancing 0.64% and 0.8%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Evercore ISI upgrades Procter & Gamble

Procter & Gamble was upgraded to Outperform from In line by Evercore, which raised its PT to $166 from $161, citing improving U.S. execution, stabilizing category volumes, and signs that the company’s new organization is beginning to deliver.

Analyst Robert Ottenstein raised its fiscal first-quarter organic sales growth estimate to about 3%, versus a consensus of 2%, saying the quarter could mark the “end of downside risk” to P&G’s sales. They also expect the company to exit fiscal 2027 growing about 4%, a pace it said should support operating leverage.

Palatir upgraded on recent underperformance

Palantir was upgraded by Goldman Sachs from Neutral to Buy, citing recent underperformance.

“The two key debates we hear from investors at Palantir's current $8B revenue run rate and ~100% growth rate are 1) has the best part of Palantir's AI opportunity already been realized, or is the market deep enough for another set of higher revisions? And 2) how sustainable is the FDE model? Our primary takeaway from our most recent set of industry conversations is that the stock is setting up for another phase of outperformance into 2027,” said analyst Gabriela Borges.

The brokerage put a PT of $230 on the stock.

GlobalFoundries downgraded by BNP Paribas

GlobalFoundries was downgraded by BNP Paribas to Neutral from Outperform as the investment firm said it sees the growth drivers for the semiconductor foundry as “priced in.”

“We remain optimistic on GlobalFoundries' growth plan and capability to diversify into higher margin optical, satcom, and automotive power applications,” BNP analyst Karl Ackerman wrote. “However, we believe these will be more gradual than current projections. Coupled with structural headwinds limiting Smart Mobile growth, we take a more conservative approach to the company's growth outlook.”

Ackerman also cut his price target to $51 from $80, adding that geopolitical concerns may be a concern for the company.

SentinelOne downgraded on CrowdStrike concerns

SentinelOne was downgraded to Sector Perform from Outperform at FBN Securities, as the investment firm cited concerns about CrowdStrike encroaching on its business.

“The business has improved – NG operating margin% reached a record 10.5% in FQ2 2027, RPO accelerated to 45% Y/Y and AI security ARR roughly tripled – but at $25.43 the shares have moved through our target and more than doubled from the April low, while CrowdStrike keeps taking a larger share of incremental ARR than S’s share of the installed base,” FBN analyst Shebly Seyrafi wrote in a note to clients. “Net, we see a balanced risk/reward from here.”

BNP Paribas raised its Nvidia price target to $345 from $285, citing the company's broad range of AI hardware, CUDA software, and networking products. The brokerage also raised Intel's price target to $125 from $75 while maintaining a Neutral rating, saying it could benefit from rising demand for server CPUs as AI agents require more computing power.

Citi upped its price target on AMD to $800 from $575 as the investment firm said it now sees the CPU market hitting $300B by 2030.

data.title: AI euphoria faces concern as bubble warnings intensify
data.description:
The artificial-intelligence boom has sent the market roaring but now several analysts, investors, and policymakers are warning that the bubble may be approaching its breaking point.

Concerns that initially centered on skyrocketing corporate debt to finance the massive data centers and rising interest rates have since escalated, with industry leaders now saying that advances in AI could potentially cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade.

In an unusual display of solidarity, the heads of many AI labs came together last month to say that the progress of improving AI model capabilities should be scaled back.

In the face of potential risks, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called to 'slow the pace' of AI model improvements and urged for greater coordination among AI companies, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk agreeing with Amodei. This came after an Anthropic insider Evan Hubinger said in a post on X that he "earnestly" believes AI could kill all humans, putting his personal estimate of the probability at more than 10% within the next decade.

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates also stated that the technology is “powerful enough” to help cause at least 1B human deaths. This week, Anthropic , OpenAI , and other companies’ top executives are reportedly gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt following a catastrophic AI event.

Here are some prominent investors, strategists, and analysts who warned that the AI bubble could burst

Ray Dalio

The billionaire has sounded the alarm on the AI bubble, warning that it is nearing the point where it may burst due to rising interest rates and increased borrowing to fund the AI infrastructure buildout.

"What creates the bursting of a bubble is the fact that you need cash," he said. "And you start to convert the wealth that you have to do that. Something like a wealth tax would have that effect, or having to pay back loans. So there's that dynamic that we have to keep an eye on."

Joachim Klement:

The London investment-bank strategist sees a scenario in which the AI-driven rally unravels as soon as 2027, dragging the broader market sharply lower.

“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview and urged clients to prepare for such a scenario rather than wait for the selloff to begin.

Michael Burry

The famous “Big Short” investor caution that the AI boom could resemble past speculative market episodes. He took short positions against high-flying tech and industrial stocks, including Nvidia , Oracle , Palantir , Nebius , Micron , CoreWeave , and has repeatedly challenged the AI investment narrative. He has argued that enormous capital spending might not necessarily translate into durable returns.

Michael Novogratz

The Galaxy Digital CEO said it is in the "biggest bubble of our lifetime" but advised investors to ride the wave rather than exit immediately.

Sam Altman:  

Last year, the OpenAI CEO has reportedly said that he believes AI could be in a bubble and compared the market conditions to those of the dotcom boom in the 1990s.

"Are we in a phase where investors as a whole are overexcited about AI? My answer is yes," Altman told tech media The Verge.

Steve Eisman 

Another legendary investor behind "The Big Short," warned that the stock market would "go straight down" if any major tech hyperscaler cuts its AI capital expenditures. He reportedly warned that a failure of major AI companies like OpenAI could trigger an immediate U.S. recession due to extreme market dependence on AI.

Gary MarcusIn his Substack account, the cognitive scientist and author in 2025 wrote that “If September 2025 was peak bubble, 2026 will likely the year which it all falls apart.”
David CahnSequoia’s David Cahn put the annual gap between AI infrastructure spending and ecosystem revenue at nearly $600 billion. He said the AI bubble is reaching “a tipping point.”
Ben Inker

The GMO co-head of asset allocation during one CNBC interview said that “AI is a bubble, and figuring out exactly when it’s going to burst is really hard.” He added that AI boom relies heavily on debt and "circular deals" where money-losing firms fund one another's infrastructure.

Ryan Hammond

The Goldman Sachs strategist in 2025 reportedly warned investors AI remains a powerful long-term theme but warned that near-term risks are mounting. He highlighted that investors demanding much more scrutiny about massive hyperscaler capital expenditure as well as tangible evidence about its returns.

data.title: Cirrus Logic is said to have made a rival bid for Synaptics after Onsemi offer
data.description:
Cirrus Logic has offered to acquire Synaptics in September, as the semiconductor company looked to fend off a competing bid from ON Semiconductor Corporation , Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The report came after onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in an all-cash deal worth roughly $5.7B last week, revising its previous all-stock bid worth about $7B disclosed in June.

Onsemi changed the deal terms following an “unsolicited competing proposal” from a third party, according to a statement, which didn’t name the bidder.

Austin-based Cirrus Logic is the "Party A" mentioned in an updated proxy filing from Synaptics on Thursday, the people said, asking for anonymity as details are private.

The filing indicated that board members of Synaptics seriously evaluated Cirrus Logic’s cash and stock bid and even held discussions with the company before eventually settling on Onsemi's revised offer.

It’s unclear if Cirrus Logic continues to have buyout interest in Synaptics, the people added.

Representatives for both Cirrus Logic and Onsemi declined to comment on the report, according to Bloomberg. Synaptics didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: America's hottest pizza chains might be gas station operators
data.description:
Convenience stores and gas stations across the country are increasingly serving up made-to-order pizza that rivals what customers get from traditional pizzerias in a phenomenon that is starting to reshape the competitive map for the industry. A recent pizza-industry research report noted that gas station pizza, long dismissed as low-quality food hardening all day under heat lamps, is improving enough that it's now considered a serious and fast-rising competitor eating into pizzeria profits, especially in small towns without as many dine-in and delivery options.

Casey's General Stores , which operates roughly 2,600 locations across the Midwest and beyond, has leaned heavily into low-cost fresh food offerings, including pizza and bakery items. Notably, Casey's built its pizza business by turning convenience stores into neighborhood pizzerias, particularly in small towns underserved by major restaurant chains. By installing on-site ovens and kitchens rather than simply selling reheated pizza, the convenience store chain has established a reputation for serving quality pizza and boosted customer loyalty. The pizza business expanded alongside Casey’s store network through a rural strategy that includes new construction, acquisitions, and investments in kitchens. The company also developed its own distribution network, helping maintain consistent supplies and control logistics costs across locations.

Also in the mix, Hunt Brothers Pizza is a family-owned, Nashville-based pizza business founded in 1991 by four brothers. Rather than operating stand-alone restaurants, the company supplies a branded pizza program to convenience stores and gas stations, particularly in rural communities with limited restaurant options. The chain is now found in more than 11K locations across 33 states. While quality can vary across locations, Hunt Brothers scores very high on consumer review sites in comparison to national pizza chains.

Over the last year, Domino's has snapped up market share from rivals such as Pizza Hut and Papa John's even as it faces the new threat in rural areas from the gas station operators with updated pizza ovens.

data.title: The Real Challenge For Muse AI Is Making The Math Make Sense — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Levine

Meta Platforms' Muse personal AI agent is an early hit, holding the iOS App Store top spot since soon after its Sept. 8 release. According to research from Human Security, it was already the No. 1 agent last month, responsible for 40% of agent-based traffic on the internet. Largely because of its release, agent traffic tripled in a month.

Meta stock is up 18% since Muse's release.

But Meta is probably losing money on Muse now, and it will be very hard for it to defray the costs down the line.

As it demonstrated with its Threads microblogging platform, Meta's strategy is to scale a new product and then monetize it with ads. But Muse may be different, because it's promising to bring a level of privacy and security to it that Meta isn't known for. Soon, interactions with Muse will be opaque to everyone aside from the user, including Meta. The kind of highly effective ad targeting that Meta's data collection enables in Facebook and Instagram may not work as well in Muse. If user behavior in Muse is anonymized, it won't provide Meta with data to further refine its targeting.

In any case, Meta isn't yet talking about ads in Muse. For now, it is looking to e-commerce and premium subscriptions to subsidize the costs.

And those costs may be very high. At least to begin with, Meta is being very generous with the Muse free tier, allocating up to 100 million tokens a week for each user. Tokens are the basic unit of artificial-intelligence text; for example, this sentence is made up of about 30 tokens when measured by common methods. Though we don't know exactly what the computing costs of 100 million tokens are to Meta, we have a decent idea of what it would charge if someone were using the underlying model, Muse Spark, to do other things like writing software code using the company's application programming interface, or API.

On the API, there are different prices for tokens depending on how they are being used, with the cheapest being "cache" tokens. Even if 97% of a Muse user's tokens are for cache, free-tier users are getting the equivalent of an $1,100 annual API credit. In the past 12 months, Meta has generated only $63.54 per each of its 3.6 billion daily app users, almost entirely through ads. The tough job ahead of Meta is bridging that gap for Muse.

It's unclear what Meta's profit margin is on the Muse Spark API, but we can deduce that it isn't as high as the top models from OpenAI and Anthropic. In the "cost per task" metric of research firm Artificial Analysis, Muse Spark is closer to inexpensive Chinese models than the ones from the U.S. frontier AI labs. The Muse Spark API is a great deal for users, and Meta may well be underpricing it to gain market share.

Revenue per user from the Muse agent is likely going to have to be much higher than what Meta earns from its apps to recoup the costs. If Meta were able to capture all of Visa's revenue with its Muse e-commerce fees — $45 billion in the past 12 months — that could be enough, but scaling to the size of Visa won't be easy.

This year, Meta intends to spend up to $145 billion on capital expenditures for new AI data centers.

The Muse math gets even tougher for Meta in the paid tiers. The $240-a-year plan offers the equivalent of $5,500 in annual API credit, and the $1,200-a-year tier comes with a staggering $33,000 of annual credit. On the free tier, where most of the casual users of Muse will be, Meta can count on many of them not coming close to their free token allocation, bringing average token use down. But people on the paid plans will likely be power users who will be using Muse to run their lives like a full-time human personal assistant would. They may come close to using up their entire token budget every week.

Meta didn't respond to a request for comment on the wide gulf between its average revenue per user and Muse token allocations.

The company is hoping that everyone becomes a power user, and that they make Muse a daily habit like its social-media apps. But the more successful Muse is, and the more people use it, the more difficult profitability will become.

This dovetails with a recent report from research firm SemiAnalysis, which showed that the API costs of the token allocations for OpenAI and Anthropic subscription plans are well in excess of their subscription prices. In effect, at all three companies, API customers are subsidizing free and subscription users.

The situation is indicative of where we are right now in AI. The costs are evident in the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent for new AI data centers. Cloud providers like Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Alphabet are earning revenue from renting out these servers, but companies with no cloud service like Meta are fishing around for income, and it isn't clear exactly where the profits come from when the expenses are so high.

Meanwhile, Meta shareholders have to endure reduced operating profit margins, down to 37% in the latest quarter (after excluding some one-time charges) from 43% last year. Making Muse a mass-market service is going to be no mean feat, but making it a profitable one may prove the bigger hill to climb.

data.title: ED arrests Sadhna Group MD over money-laundering allegations: Who is Rakesh Gupta? What's the Rs.168 crore case?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Dr Rakesh Gupta, chairman and managing director of Sadhna Group, has been arrested. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has detailed him in a money-laundering case involving alleged criminal proceeds. The agency estimates these proceeds at about Rs.168 crore.

A court sent Gupta to five days of ED custody early on 10 October. Gupta's arrest took place at Ishwar Farms. The group runs Sadhna TV and other media networks.

Gupta, 63, is the founder, chairman and managing director of Delhi-based Sadhna Group. The group operates channels covering spiritual programmes, culture and regional news.

These include Sadhna TV, Ishwar TV, Sadhna Plus News and Har Khabar. Sadhna TV has over 3.9 million subscribers on YouTube.

Gupta has a YouTube channel called "The Dr Rakesh Gupta Show Plus Minus". He presents himself as a senior journalist and mentor. The YouTube channel has 18,700 subscribers.

His programmes cover motivational stories, startups, UPSC success and ancient Indian history. They also highlight local innovators and businesspeople who address social problems. On social media, he invites young entrepreneurs to share business ideas.

His business interests include a Bio-CNG plant in Mathura, solar installations and outdoor advertising. His companies also hold marketing rights across various metro stations.

The ED investigation follows a Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing FIR registered on 29 September. The police case includes allegations of cheating and criminal breach of trust. Gupta is named as the second accused.

The ED alleges that Gupta arranged Sadhna Media Pvt Ltd's insolvency through connected creditors. Such creditors held 99.41% of the committee of creditors. According to ED, income-tax dues of Rs.110.10 crore were settled for Rs.20 lakh.

The agency alleges that the company paid Rs.4.48 crore to connected creditors. This included about Rs.2.99 crore paid to Gupta's company, Sharpline Broadcast Ltd.

It also alleges cash receipts of Rs.2.50 crore to Rs.2.82 crore. These allegedly came through USDT and hawala channels during SMPL/Aryan TV's resale.

The ED further cited a SEBI order concerning alleged Sadhna Broadcast Ltd share manipulation. It said SEBI identified Gupta as the mastermind and held him, along with others, liable. The amount involved was about Rs.58 crore.

Investigators want to trace cash, examine seized devices and check company records. They also seek details about Rs.8.98 crore payable without any bank trail.

The court granted five days' custody, considering Gupta's age and the specific tasks of the investigation. He must appear again on 15 October by 4 PM.

data.title: Zomato, Blinkit Host EV Bazaar To Expand Electric Two-Wheeler Adoption
data.description:
Third edition sees 2,500 delivery partners and 20+ EV manufacturers and ecosystem partners participate in new delhi

Eternal-owned Zomato and Blinkit hosted the third edition of EV Bazaar in New Delhi on 9 October, bringing together 2,500 delivery partners and more than 20 electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers and ecosystem partners to encourage the use of electric two-wheelers for deliveries.

Held at KD Jadhav Stadium, the event allowed delivery partners to compare and test-ride more than 30 electric two-wheeler models and explore options for buying or renting vehicles. The event also brought together government representatives and companies offering financing, charging and battery-swapping services.

More Than 2 Lakh Delivery Partners Use EVs

As of 30 September 2026, more than 200,000 delivery partners across Zomato and Blinkit were using electric two-wheelers, according to Eternal. In FY26, electric vehicles powered 228 million deliveries across the two platforms, avoiding an estimated 9,926 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions.

Anjalli Ravi Kumar, Chief Sustainability Officer at Eternal, said the decision to switch to an electric two-wheeler was both a financial and practical consideration for delivery partners, whose earnings depend partly on vehicle performance and availability.

EV Bazaar gives riders an opportunity to compare vehicles and interact directly with companies offering rental, financing, charging and battery-swapping services, she said.

Rental Options Aim To Lower Entry Costs

Zomato and Blinkit offer a ‘Rent a vehicle’ feature through their delivery partner apps, allowing riders to use electric two-wheelers without paying the full upfront cost of ownership. The feature also helps them locate nearby charging and battery-swapping stations within their delivery zones.

More than 23,000 delivery partners used the feature to rent electric vehicles for deliveries in FY26. Separately, Zomato Local Services Private Limited launched its own EV rental fleet in June 2025, with more than 1,500 electric two-wheelers deployed across Delhi and Chennai as of March 2026.

Charging And Swapping Infrastructure Key

Mahmood Ahmed, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, said wider EV adoption among delivery partners could help expand charging, battery-swapping and servicing networks, benefiting other users as well.

The event also recognised delivery partners contributing to the transition, with three receiving new electric two-wheelers and another receiving a one-year free rental plan.

data.title: India’s GCC Boom Accelerates As 111 New Centres Open Between January And August 2026
data.description:
Global companies are expanding technology, finance, data and AI operations across Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Noida and other Indian hubs

India’s global capability centre (GCC) ecosystem continued to expand in 2026, with 111 new greenfield centres opening between January and August, surpassing the 100 centres established during the whole of 2025, according to an September 2026 report by ENN Business.

The report highlights expansion plans and new setups by global companies across sectors, including steel, life sciences, aviation, chemicals, healthcare, insurance and entertainment. The developments reflect growing investment in technology, data, artificial intelligence (AI), finance and other business functions in India.

Hyderabad emerged as a leading destination, accounting for 40 of the 111 new GCCs opened during the first eight months of 2026, according to the report. The National Capital Region (NCR) also strengthened its position, accounting for 45 per cent of GCC absorption in 2025, compared with 18 per cent in 2024.

Global Firms Expand Across Cities

Among the major developments, ArcelorMittal is planning to hire 2,000 professionals across Hyderabad and Pune as its AMGBT operations scale up in phases. The roles are expected to span digital technology, IT infrastructure, data analytics, cybersecurity, finance, procurement and human resources.

Merck Group is developing an integrated campus at Electronic City in Bengaluru, bringing together teams across functions. The report puts the centre’s scale at 3,300 professionals, with work spanning data, digital, process and technology functions.

In Hyderabad, Southwest Airlines opened its first centre outside the United States on 20 May 2026, with plans to hire 1,000 technology professionals. Its focus areas include AI, analytics and cybersecurity.

BASF is establishing two hubs in Hyderabad: a Global Digital Hub and a Global Service Hub covering finance and HR. The report lists the developments across the first and second quarters of 2026.

LG Electronics is planning a Rs 1,000 crore Phase II campus across seven acres in Noida, in the NCR region. The expansion is expected to create 500 jobs, with 90 per cent local hiring highlighted in the report.

Life Sciences And Digital Operations

The report also identifies Hyderabad as a destination for expansion in life sciences and business services. The HEINEKEN Company is setting up a 76,000 sq. ft. centre described as its first in the Asia-Pacific region. Its functions are expected to include finance, procurement, supply chain, HR, digital and data.

Swiss life sciences company Lonza is establishing a GCC in Hyderabad focused on operational, digital and scientific functions supporting pharmaceutical and biotechnology businesses. The report notes that the company recorded sales of CHF 6.5 billion in 2025.

Healthcare technology company Cohere Health announced its Hyderabad centre on 26 February 2026. It expects to build a team of approximately 350 people over six to seven quarters, with a focus on clinical AI for health-plan operations.

Technology Work Moves In-House

Technology operations are another area of expansion. The Standard is moving towards bringing engineering work in-house, shifting technology responsibilities away from external vendors. The report notes its presence at Embassy Tech Village in Bengaluru and its entry into India six months earlier.

The Walt Disney Company is also expanding its existing technology centre in Bengaluru, bringing more engineering work in-house that was previously handled by IT vendors.

Hyderabad And NCR In Focus

The report’s figures point to the continued concentration of GCC activity in established technology and business hubs. Hyderabad accounted for 40 new centres between January and August 2026, while NCR’s share of GCC absorption increased significantly in 2025.

The developments across the 10 companies span technology, cybersecurity, AI, analytics, finance, procurement, HR, supply chain and scientific operations. They also indicate that GCCs are being developed for a range of business functions, beyond traditional technology support.

With 111 greenfield centres opening in the first eight months of 2026, India’s GCC market has already exceeded the number of new centres reported for the whole of 2025, according to ENN Business.

data.title: U.S. issues AI reporting mandate after Anthropic breaches: Axios
data.description:
The White House has issued a mandate requiring all artificial intelligence companies to notify and correct security incidents after Anthropic reported a series of breaches involving one of its AI models, according to Axios.

“This notification and remediation process is not optional," White House Super Intelligence Force leaders said in a statement, adding, "It is a critical national security obligation."

The maker of the Claude AI model contacted the State Department on Thursday to disclose breaches regarding “unauthorized and fraudulent use of government and other systems,” the officials said.

The incidents, including one where an Anthropic testing model submitted a series of non-immigrant visa applications in May and August, were discovered late last month, and they have ceased since then, the government said.

"SI companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm," the statement added. "We also expect these companies to work with the affected systems to ensure that similar incidents do not occur."

Separately on Friday, Anthropic published a report acknowledging that Claude submitted a false tip about an unsolved homicide to police and made other unintended actions on third-party systems.

In a statement, the Philadelphia Police Department said that the bogus tip was made in July via PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a website where people can share information about unsolved murders.

Anthropic’s report outlined several other previously undisclosed breaches, which the company categorized into four groups, including unauthorized submission of a sensitive form on a real website.

The company said that the violations were “significantly less severe” than the cybersecurity incidents it reported in July and September. “The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact,” Anthropic added.

The incident marks the latest in a series of breaches the company and its rival OpenAI have reported in recent months, prompting concerns over the safety of rapid AI development from experts both within and outside the industry.

data.title: One year after $19 billion crash, crypto faces a new reality
data.description:
A year ago, crypto was riding a wave of White House support, Wall Street enthusiasm and expectations of a new golden age. Then came October’s historic crash, wiping out a record $19 billion in leveraged bets in a single day, setting off an industry-wide retrenchment and exposing the fragility of a market structure supposedly coming of age.

Twelve months later, market bellwether Bitcoin remains more than 30% below its record high. Attempts at a sustained rally have repeatedly faltered and traders have been slow to rebuild the leveraged positions that once powered crypto’s biggest booms.

Total open interest in Bitcoin-linked perpetual futures -- a gauge of traders’ appetite for leveraged bets -- stood at about $45 billion a year ago, according to CryptoQuant data. It more than halved in the six months after the crash. Bitcoin’s recent rally above $80,000 restored some confidence, but open interest in the world’s biggest token remains well off its peak.

Still, the malaise hasn’t stopped banks and major trading firms from experimenting with digital assets. More important than whether leverage returns is whether the market itself has become more resilient, said Julia Zhou, president at crypto market maker Caladan.

“More than $19 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated within 24 hours, but the bigger issue was how quickly available liquidity disappeared when the market needed it most,” Zhou said. Today, while traders understand the risks better, “the market remains highly fragmented, and liquidity can still deteriorate rapidly,” she added.

The case for a stronger market today is that leverage is lower, exchanges offer less-correlated assets and some venues have beefed up liquidation systems.

Meanwhile, investors haven’t lost their taste for gambling, but have turned to new frontiers. Prediction markets are drawing crowds, and perpetual futures or “perps” — long a staple of crypto trading — are being used to place leveraged bets on stocks, commodities and other real-world assets. Put another way, some of the very machinery that helped turn crypto into a speculative phenomenon is finding uses well beyond the tokens it was designed to trade: Wall Street is forging ahead with stablecoins, tokenization and the financial infrastructure built on blockchain technology.

Open interest in perpetual futures for real-world assets, virtually non-existent a year ago, today stands at more than $17 billion, according to DefiLlama data. Much of that has been driven by Hyperliquid, the offshore crypto exchange, which was an early mover in tying perps to stocks and commodities.

The shift “tells a growth story of people that want yield and settlement on rails that never close, not from people chasing a narrative or a buzzy memecoin,” said Adam McCarthy, head of research at trading firm LO:TECH.

The never-ending quest for higher returns helped make Bitcoin the world’s best-performing financial asset since its inception 17 years ago. For long-time crypto-market participants, the increased institutionalization of the sector and corresponding rise of fresh alternatives from perpetual futures to sports betting are seen as an inflection point.

In a report released this week, QCP Capital said it expected Bitcoin to be stuck in a range of $80,000 to $90,000 in the fourth quarter. The structural case for crypto remains intact, but flows alone aren’t enough without a dominant catalyst, the firm wrote.

A year out, the market looks fundamentally different, Galaxy Digital said in a report Friday. Despite the failure of US crypto regulation in September, federal regulators are moving ahead with plans to strengthen trading with guidelines over the use of collateral and margin.

All that means an industry born of disruptive idealism and defined by speculative excess is becoming more closely integrated with the financial establishment it once sought to displace. And with artificial intelligence commanding much of the market’s imagination, crypto faces a different future from the one envisioned in its early boom years: less a rebellion against Wall Street than another corner of it.

“For the most part, the market that crashed on 10/10 doesn’t really exist anymore,” wrote Lucas Tcheyan, vice president of research at Galaxy Digital. “The one that replaced it is just starting to get priced in.”

data.title: The Real Challenge For Muse AI Is Making The Math Make Sense — Barrons.com
Winter is coming and energy bills are climbing. 'Everything just keeps going up.'
data.description:
By Myra P. Saefong and Andrew Keshner

Utilities want to raise your rates even more

Household heating costs are set to pile up this winter.

Carolina Bustos has a nighttime routine. When it's after 9 p.m., it's time to turn on her dishwasher and crank up her air conditioner to cool down the Houston nights.

By running the appliances in off-peak hours, the tactic is supposed to save her money.

Still, in the past two months, she says her electricity bill has doubled, up to at least $400.

"Everything just keeps going up," Bustos told MarketWatch. She's been leaning on her credit cards more to make ends meet. "I'm not too sure there's anything I can do."

Expensive utility bills have become an increasingly sharp thorn for Americans' wallets, but warmer weather this winter and energy assistance programs can help.

Average heating costs for U.S. households are expected to rise by 8.3% this winter compared to last winter, according to a recent report from the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, a policy group for state directors of the federal Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program.

Those who use heating oil to heat their homes, however, may see their costs rise by 50% this winter, the report said.

Families are facing an "energy affordability crisis," said Mark Wolfe, executive director of NEADA, with electricity prices continuing to rise faster than inflation and households using heating oil for heat facing an "extraordinary price shock."

At the same time, utilities across the country have requested $23 billion in rate increases through September. This includes a record-breaking $4.5 billion in rate increases during the third quarter, according to PowerLines, a consumer-education organization.

For working families and seniors living on Social Security, "there simply isn't enough room in the household budget to absorb increases of this magnitude," said Wolfe.

The forecasts and rate-hike requests come in a midterm-election season where everyday living costs are a major campaign theme.

Utility costs are up there with healthcare, gas prices and food costs when it comes to consumers' affordability worries, a KFF poll showed Tuesday. Half of voters said they were at least somewhat worried about paying for monthly utilities, including 18% who said they were "very worried" about being able to afford the necessary costs.

It could be a while before the latest rounds of rate-hike requests filter into utility bills, said Charles Hua, founder and executive director of PowerLines. It's still not clear how many public-utility commissions will ultimately approve of the requests.

But higher prices are coming in some form.

Electricity costs tied to heating for the winter - from mid-October to mid-March - are expected to climb by 7.2% from last year, according to NEADA.

Out of all the heating sources, however, it estimates that households using heating oil will be the hardest hit, paying about 50% more in heating costs than last winter. It expects the average household to pay $2,627 this winter to heat a home with heating oil, up $878 from last winter as wars in Iran and Ukraine have disrupted petroleum markets and pushed heating-oil prices sharply higher.

The Energy Information Administration, however, forecasts a smaller 19% rise in heating bills, to an average of $1,794 this winter for U.S. households using heating oil to heat their homes, in part citing assumptions for warmer temperatures in the Northeast, where about 82% of U.S. households use heating oil as their primary heating fuel.

Super El Niño's silver lining? It depends.

A potentially historic El Niño weather pattern may take some sting out of winter utility bills. But that's no guarantee and it depends where people live, experts said.

It could be the strongest El Niño since 1950, according to AccuWeather. That could mean above-average temperatures in most of America's northern states, according to its winter forecast.

Parts of Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan could see seven- to nine-degree higher average winter temperatures compared to last year, said Paul Pastelok, AccuWeather's lead U.S. long-range forecaster. That's where heating bills could potentially get the most help from milder temperatures, he said.

Yet lower heating demand may not mean paying less, due to energy prices and household energy use, AccuWeather said.

People in Upper Midwest states might pay less, but households in Southern and Gulf Coast states might end up paying more, said Alexis Abramson, dean of the Columbia Climate School. The weather pattern may produce wetter weather, which could be colder.

Many households in the region tend to be heated by electricity, she noted. "Electricity prices are up in most parts of the country. Definitely in that part of the country."

Utilities in Southern states asked for $2.2 billion in rate hikes during the third quarter, according to PowerLines, comprising the steepest requests in the country.

Cost burdens - especially for heating fuel

Still, heating-oil prices near record highs are hard to ignore.

Heating oil costs around $6.19 a gallon, close to double the mid-$3 range it was priced at on Jan. 1, said Ken Williams, president and owner of Scott-Williams, Inc., a heating-fuel delivery and heating and cooling installation, maintenance and repair company based in Quincy, Mass.

Household heating-oil fuel tanks hold about 275 gallons, with a medium-sized home getting around three deliveries of 200 gallons each per year, he said. That means the cost of one delivery has climbed from around $700 to just over $1,200.

Some customers might have paid each delivery cost in full, but in order to help them manage the price increase, Williams said his company has shifted customers to monthly payment plans so the costs are easier to absorb and customers have a better idea of what to expect to pay each month.

Nationwide, there are programs that help households with energy costs to meet winter heating needs.

Energy assistance comes in the form of U.S. dollars, not gallons, so with the higher prices for heating oil, 'those dollars are only going to go half as far as they did a year ago.'Ken Williams, Scott-Williams, Inc.

In Maine, which is among the states most dependent on heating oil, the state's housing authority, aka MaineHousing, administers the federal Low-Income Energy Assistance Program. It helps around 35,000 to 40,000 households a year manage their energy costs, with assistance approval based on income, said Scott Thistle, communications director at MaineHousing. For the state, a household of four earning less than a median annual income of $73,213 would qualify.

Maine's energy assistance program is designed to give each eligible household a "meaningful" dollar benefit amount, said Thistle. But when the price of fuel approaches $7 a gallon, then the "purchasing power of that benefit amount goes way down, and the amount of fuel somebody gets goes way down."

Heating-oil dealer Williams said energy assistance comes in the form of U.S. dollars, not gallons, so with the higher prices, "those dollars are only going to go half as far as they did a year ago."

-Myra P. Saefong -Andrew Keshner

data.title: Bitcoin rally restores some confidence, but open interest lags
data.description:
Bitcoin has staged a comeback. The leverage crowd mostly stayed home.

The world's largest crypto asset climbed approximately 35% from its August 2026 lows around $63,500, reaching the $83,000 to $84,000 range by late September. Futures open interest has not kept pace, however, and remains below its previous high.

Open interest measures the total value of outstanding futures contracts that haven't been closed or settled. When it rises alongside price, traders are piling in with fresh bets. When it falls during a rally, the table is getting quieter even as the score improves.

That second scenario is what played out here. Measured in BTC terms, futures open interest fell nearly 20% during the run-up.

Analysts at Bitfinex flagged that aggregate BTC futures open interest dropped to approximately 625,000 BTC. That marks a significant pullback in leveraged positioning, and a notable low for 2026.

Denominating open interest in BTC rather than dollars is a useful filter. A rising price can inflate dollar-based open interest even if nobody opens a new contract. Counting in coins strips that effect out and shows whether positioning itself is growing or shrinking.

A chunk of that decline traces back to a single day. On August 19, 2026, a liquidation event swept through the derivatives market, with 85% of the liquidations hitting short positions.

Open interest contracted by 11% shortly after that event.

Beyond the squeeze, the rally appears to have been powered by spot market demand. Reports point to institutional inflows into exchange-traded funds and short covering, rather than traders opening new leveraged long positions.

Into early October, Bitcoin settled into a range between $82,000 and $85,000. ETF flows moved back and forth, and open interest stopped falling and began to stabilize.

Across trading venues, broader perpetual futures open interest sat between $35 billion and $54 billion in notional terms during that stretch.

Lower leverage cuts both ways. On the plus side, fewer overextended positions means less fuel for a sudden liquidation cascade.

The trade-off is speed. Leverage is what usually turns a solid rally into an explosive one. Without renewed derivatives participation, the potential for sharp, rapid price gains looks limited unless new capital enters the market.

For traders, ETF flow data is likely the most important signal to watch. The October range between $82,000 and $85,000 coincided with swings in those flows, which suggests institutional demand is effectively setting the pace.

Open interest is the second gauge. A gradual rebuild in BTC-denominated open interest alongside steady spot demand would point to renewed conviction. A sudden surge in leverage without matching spot buying would revive the old fragility the market just spent months shedding.

The research frames the current setup as reason for cautious optimism. Rising prices, reduced leverage, and steady institutional participation could add up to more sustainable growth, punctuated by occasional bouts of volatility.

data.title: RBI opens special USD window for these 3 state-run OMCs; facility in effect from Oct 12 - What it means for INR support?

USD vs INR, Oct. 10 -- In a bid to support the Indian National Rupee (INR) against the US Dollar (USD), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has opened a special facility for the three state-run Oil Manufacturing Companies (OMCs). The facility will take effect on Monday, 12th October 2026.

In this facility, the three oil PSUs - Indian Oil Corporation Ltd, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd - will be able to meet the entire daily dollar requirement for oil purchases. The RBI made this announcement on Saturday, 10 October 2026.

The RBI made this announcement on Saturday, saying, "On the basis of an assessment of current market conditions, the Reserve Bank of India has decided to open a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), viz. Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. Under the facility, the Reserve Bank will undertake the sale of USD to the public sector OMCs through designated bank/s. The facility will take effect on October 12, 2026 (Monday) and remain in place until further notice.

As mentioned above, the dollar window will be available for just three state-run OMCs - IOCL, HPCL, and BPCL.

On how these three OMCs will be able to contain the Indian Rupee's fall amid soaring crude oil prices, Sandeep Pandey, Co-founder of Basav Capital, said, "If you look at the percentage share of these three oil PSUs in the net petroleum products sale in India, they constitute around 90%. IOCL covers the maximum 40% shares, followed by the 30% share of BPCL and 20% share of HPCL. So, the petroleum product's sales data is enough to understand the share they have in the oil imports."

On how this RBI's move will lend support to the weak Indian Rupee, Sandeep Pandey said, "In the current market system, oil companies need to buy the USD from the open market by converting the Indian Rupee into the USD, then they pay for the oil imports from the international markets. However, under the current system, OMCs will now buy USD from designated Indian banks rather than in the open market."

The Basav Capital expert said that the Government of India (GoI) has now opened a window for the three OMCs to convert the Indian Rupee into the US dollar and vice versa.

On how the GoI will be able to meet this additional USD demand, Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said, "The GoI has recently launched the FCNR bonds, which are a big hit. So, the USD received from FCNR bonds would be the primary source of USD for the Indian government. They can also generate USD by converting the deposits' swap.

data.title: Beyond gold and diamonds: The changing business of luxury jewellery in India
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- When a woman tries on a piece of high jewellery, what makes her want to own it? Is it the diamonds, the precious stones, the craftsmanship, or the value of the materials? For Ajoy Chawla, MD, Titan Company Limited, the answer increasingly lies in something less tangible: how the piece makes her feel.

"You can see it in her eyes. The desire is in her eyes," Chawla said in an interview with Mint, describing the experience of watching a customer try on an exceptional piece of jewellery. The moment, he suggested, is not simply about how she looks in it, but also about what wearing it makes her feel.

It is a useful way to understand the changing business of luxury jewellery in India. In a market where gold has long represented wealth, security and tradition, an emerging premium consumer is also looking for individuality, original design and a stronger emotional connection with what she buys.

That shift is creating an opportunity for organised jewellery brands to move beyond selling precious materials and build a more differentiated proposition around design, craftsmanship and brand identity.The Signature Couture Edit, brought to India for the first time by Tanishq Natural Diamonds through an exclusive, invite-only exhibition in Mumbai, offers a glimpse into this evolution. Following its unveiling at Paris Couture Week 2026, the collection was co-designed with internationally acclaimed couturier Rahul Mishra, translating the narratives of haute couture into high jewellery.

Drawing inspiration from nature and architecture, the collection combines sculptural forms with natural white and black diamonds and coloured gemstones, including citrine, emerald, amethyst, pink tourmaline, rubellite and garnet. Pieces such as Enchanted Canopy and Imperial Cascade Neckwear bring together intricate detailing and expressive silhouettes, positioning jewellery as an extension of a designer's creative language.

For Chawla, the collection reflects a broader change in consumer aspirations. "India is ready for designers. India is really ready for luxury. India is ready for high jewellery," he said.

His observation also points to a business opportunity: serving consumers who are increasingly willing to explore luxury through distinctive Indian design, rather than viewing it exclusively through the lens of established international brands.

India's jewellery market is large, but its organised segment still has considerable room to expand. Deloitte's January 2025 report, Sparkling Success: Renaissance in India's Gems and Jewellery Sector, estimated the market at 80billion-85 billion in FY24. It projected that organised retailers' share would rise from around 36%-38% in FY24 to 42%-43% by FY28, supported by rising incomes, urbanisation and evolving consumer preferences.

For jewellery companies, growth has two dimensions: bringing more consumers into branded and diamond jewellery, and encouraging existing customers to move towards higher-value purchases.

Chawla believes both opportunities are significant. He estimated diamond-jewellery penetration in India at around 12%-14%, based on industry estimates, suggesting substantial headroom for the category. At the same time, he said average transaction values were rising not only because gold prices had increased, but also because customers were choosing more expressive pieces.

This distinction is important. Higher gold prices can increase the value of jewellery sales even when consumers buy less by weight. The World Gold Council's Gold Demand Trends: India Focus Q2 2026 reported that Indian jewellery demand fell 15% year on year to 75.1 tonnes in the April-June quarter, while its value rose 34% to Rs.1.132 trillion. The report pointed to consumers adapting to elevated prices through lighter-weight jewellery, studded designs and gold-exchange purchases.

For brands, therefore, the challenge is not simply to sell more expensive products. It is to give customers reasons to choose a particular piece beyond the underlying price of its gold and gemstones.

Designer-led collections can help create that distinction. They introduce new design languages to established retail platforms and allow brands to explore more specialised consumer segments. But their commercial value ultimately depends on whether customers see the designs as desirable, distinctive and worth the premium.

The Signature Couture Edit brings together Mishra's couture sensibility and Tanishq Natural Diamonds' jewellery design and product development capabilities. Its significance lies in how the two design perspectives are translated into pieces that consumers can experience and wear.

Jewellery in India has always carried emotional meaning. It is gifted at weddings, passed between generations and acquired to mark important milestones. What appears to be changing, particularly at the higher end of the market, is the growing importance of personal expression as a reason to buy.

"In this segment, the woman is certainly looking at jewellery as pure adornment," Chawla said.

He acknowledged that preciousness, rarity and the potential to pass a piece down the generations remain important. But he believes customers buying high jewellery are not necessarily thinking about selling it later. They are choosing something they want to wear, enjoy and perhaps eventually pass on to someone dear to them.

That perspective changes the way a brand must think about value. When a customer evaluates jewellery mainly through its gold weight or diamond content, the material composition dominates the decision. When she is drawn to a distinctive form, a particular colour or the way a piece makes her feel, design and craftsmanship become equally important.

Chawla sees growing interest in coloured gemstones as part of this shift. India, he noted, has a longstanding affinity for colour, visible in its cultural and artistic traditions. Yet premium diamond jewellery has often been associated with a predominantly white-diamond aesthetic.

He sees an opportunity to broaden that vocabulary. "There is a lot of freedom in expression even in terms of the form," he said, reflecting on the unconventional shapes and rich colours he has observed in contemporary high jewellery.

The Signature Couture Edit draws on this freedom, using natural diamonds and coloured gemstones to create sculptural compositions rather than relying exclusively on conventional silhouettes.

For consumers, such pieces can offer a way to express personal taste. For brands, they create room to differentiate collections in a category where many products can otherwise compete on similar material attributes.

The consumer shaping this market is also becoming more confident about making independent choices. Chawla observed that younger buyers are increasingly willing to select jewellery for themselves, guided by their own preferences rather than relying entirely on family members to decide what represents good value.

For this generation, value is not necessarily defined by how much gold a piece contains. It can also come from the design, the brand behind it and the extent to which it reflects the wearer's identity.

Chawla believes uniqueness and authenticity matter, particularly to younger consumers who encounter a constant stream of content and opinions online. They are looking for something that resonates with them, rather than simply following what others are buying.

He also sees limited editions appealing to this desire for distinction. Rarity can make a piece feel more personal, provided the design and brand proposition justify the purchase.

"Finally, she is buying a brand," Chawla said. "It is not a piece of jewellery. You are buying a Tanishq."

The point is not that material value has become irrelevant. Rather, the brand itself becomes part of the value equation. Consumers may find beautiful jewellery across the market, but an established brand can offer a recognisable design philosophy, consistency and confidence in the purchase.

For retailers, premiumisation therefore requires more than introducing higher-priced collections. It involves understanding what customers value, building trust and creating an experience that makes the purchase feel worthwhile.

Design is only one part of the proposition. Another challenge is helping consumers understand what they are buying.

Chawla said that even among existing diamond buyers, confusion persists about how diamonds are formed, what determines their quality and why prices vary. He believes brands need to explain the distinctive characteristics of natural diamonds, including their geological origins, rarity and optical qualities.

That education, he argued, cannot be delivered through advertising alone. Consumers need opportunities to see and understand the qualities being described.

This is a commercial consideration as much as an educational one. When consumers cannot easily distinguish between products, the credibility of the brand, the quality of information and the expertise available at the point of purchase become important differentiators.

Chawla also spoke about strengthening the identity of Tanishq's natural diamonds through assurances around selection, quality and sourcing. The broader objective is to establish a clear promise around the diamond itself, rather than relying solely on the design of the finished jewellery.

The Signature Couture Edit brings another dimension to this proposition by placing natural diamonds within a distinct creative narrative. The stones are part of a larger design statement, with their appeal shaped by how they are selected, composed and brought together.

The larger opportunity for India's jewellery industry lies in creating products that combine contemporary design with the cultural significance jewellery already holds for Indian consumers.

For Chawla, the modern Indian customer is increasingly comfortable exploring original design without feeling compelled to choose between Indian identity and a global aesthetic. The opportunity, he believes, is to serve a consumer who values authenticity and originality, whether the inspiration comes from India or elsewhere.

The Signature Couture Edit is an example of that approach. Co-designed by Tanishq Natural Diamonds and Rahul Mishra, it brings a couture design sensibility into high jewellery while retaining the significance of natural diamonds and precious gemstones.

Whether such collections translate into sustained commercial growth will depend on consumer response, pricing, and the ability to turn interest in design into purchases. But they reflect an important direction for the industry: the search for new ways to differentiate products and deepen the relationship between brands and consumers.

And for brands seeking to build the next phase of India's luxury jewellery market, answering that question could become as important as the precious materials they sell.

data.title: RBI Opens Special Dollar Window For Three State-Run Oil Marketing Companies
data.description:
The facility will meet the full daily dollar requirements of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL from 12 October, as the central bank seeks to ease pressure on the rupee

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has opened a special dollar window to meet the entire daily foreign currency requirements of three state-run oil marketing companies (OMCs), as the central bank steps up efforts to manage pressure on the rupee.

The facility will cover Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) from 12 October. Under the arrangement, the RBI will sell US dollars to the companies through designated banks.

The central bank said the facility would remain operational until further notice, based on its assessment of prevailing market conditions.

Dollar Demand Shifts Away From Spot Market

The move is intended to redirect a significant source of dollar demand away from the spot foreign exchange market. Public sector oil marketing companies require substantial amounts of foreign currency to pay for crude oil imports, making them important participants in India's dollar market.

By directly meeting their daily dollar requirements, the RBI can reduce the need for these companies to purchase dollars in the open market, potentially easing immediate pressure on the rupee.

The facility comes as the Indian currency faces sustained weakness amid elevated oil prices, global financial market pressures and demand for dollars from importers. The rupee has depreciated by more than 7 per cent this year, according to market reports.

However, the arrangement also means the RBI will supply dollars from its foreign exchange reserves, making reserve movements an important factor to monitor as the facility continues.

RBI Tightens Foreign Exchange Rules

The special window is part of a broader set of measures announced by the RBI to address volatility in the foreign exchange market. The central bank has also tightened rules governing rupee-linked foreign exchange derivatives to curb excessive speculative activity and strengthen risk management.

Among the changes, the threshold for certain derivative transactions that can be undertaken without establishing underlying exposure has been reduced from USD 100 million to USD 5 million. The RBI has also introduced restrictions on the rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts.

The measures come as the central bank seeks to contain currency volatility while maintaining orderly market conditions. While direct dollar supplies to oil companies could ease one source of demand, the rupee's trajectory will continue to depend on crude oil prices, capital flows and broader global currency movements.

data.title: Philips wins Dutch court battle with shareholders over recall
data.description:
A Dutch court on Saturday dismissed demands by shareholders of health technology company Philips for an investigation into allegations of misleading disclosures and management failures linked to the company's recall of sleep apnea devices.

  • A large group of shareholders had demanded a court inquiry, as they said Philips executives had responded too late to the problems that led to the massive recall and had failed to adequately inform investors.

  • Philips' shares lost about two thirds of their value when the company recalled around 15 million sleep apnea devices in 2021, after discovering that the foam in the machines could release harmful substances and might pose health risks.

  • The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal in its ruling said it had found no indication that Philips had known about the problems long before it issued any warning.

  • It also said there was no reason to assume executives should have intervened earlier at the Respironics subsidiary that made the devices.

  • Philips had denied the accusations made by the shareholders and said it welcomed the court's decision.

  • The sleep apnea devices recall led to probes in multiple countries, including France, where prosecutors are still investigating charges of aggravated fraud and failure to report safety risks.

  • Philips in 2024 agreed to pay $1.1 billion to settle all personal injury claims related to the devices filed in the US.
